subject.title: Feature: channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes config key to suppress message_changed / message_deleted events

question: Should Slack edit/delete events remain session-scoped system events, or should OpenClaw add an opt-in `channels.slack.ignoreSubtypes` suppression field for them?
rationale: The source behavior is clear, but the requested fix creates public Slack config surface and chooses event-context policy, which repository policy treats as maintainer/product territory rather than an automatic bug lane.

options.title: Approve narrow opt-in config
options.body: Add a documented Slack plugin `ignoreSubtypes` field, default it to current behavior, and test that only selected edit/delete subtypes are dropped before session context while Assistant DM and thread-broadcast paths still work.

options.title: Change the default policy
options.body: Stop queuing edit/delete system events by default, accepting the compatibility impact for users who currently rely on those metadata events as passive context.

options.title: Keep current system events
options.body: Decline the config key and keep edit/delete metadata flowing into session-scoped system events, with docs clarifying the current behavior and prompt-level workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow opt-in config
recommendation.body: Add a documented Slack plugin `ignoreSubtypes` field, default it to current behavior, and test that only selected edit/delete subtypes are dropped before session context while Assistant DM and thread-broadcast paths still work.

likelyOwner.reason: The Slack subtype policy history and prior broad-ignore PR decision both point to this owner as the best available decision route.
